title: Coordinated Canary Phasing Playbook for Model-Impacting Runtime Changes
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Model-impacting changes to the serving runtime (kernel updates, quantization profile swaps, KV-cache semantics) frequently require cross-surface coordination (runtime, console dashboards, API clients). We lack a single, operationally prescriptive canary phasing playbook that ties quality signals to release gates, regional windows, capacity reservations, and rollback triggers.

Goal: Create a reproducible, cross-team canary phasing playbook that standardizes: 1) signal set & thresholds (quality/e2e/telemetry), 2) phased rollout schedule and regional safe windows, 3) automated gating and pause/fallback policies, 4) runbook responsibilities and comms, and 5) post-rollout monitoring and rollback criteria. The playbook should be executable for runtime changes that affect model outputs and for console/API changes that change observability or routing behavior.

Scope: Focused on releases that can change model outputs or routing/observability behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Does NOT include purely UI cosmetic console changes. Deliverable: an operational playbook + example run (runtime-1.20 canary for gpt-open-v3) and automation checklist for release engineers.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical playbook doc exists in Confluence with step-by-step canary phases (alpha->beta->gamma), time-boxed windows, and clear owner for each step.

Defined automated metrics and thresholds documented: model-quality delta on eval set, duplicate-response rate, 99th pct latency, token-cost delta, error-rate increase; each mapped to pass/warn/fail actions.
Canary controller playbook templates for: (a) runtime kernel swap, (b) quantization profile change, (c) API routing policy update, with example commands to pause/resume and force-fallback.
Cross-surface notification templates and escalation matrix (PagerDuty & Slack) with runbook links and on-call owners for runtime/console/api teams.

A simulated canary run recorded in Playbook Demo folder (log snippets, screenshots of console traffic split, and archived eval-run) demonstrating automatic pause on quality regression and successful rollback.
Rollout automation includes a reversible fallback policy with capacity reservation knobs and a sane default slow-burn rate for multi-region rollouts.
At least two follow-up engineering tickets created (ENG-xxxx) to wire metrics into the canary controller and to add gating hooks into the console rollout switchboard.
